name: @olai/bundle
//name: THE BUILD'S SET OF PLUGINS, and the one place either tenant's name is spelled — which since the browser half followed the roster means `olai.yml` and nothing else a person edits. It was the back half of `@olai/plugin-api`, which held both the INTERFACE a plugin is written against and the REGISTRY that names every plugin — an arrangement that could not survive a plugin importing the interface, because the registry imports the plugin and the manifests decline to express a cycle. So the interface stayed where it was and the registry moved here. `bundle` is the proposal's own word for it and dsh's (a profile stacks bundles, each a list of rows plus the code they mount); it is deliberately NOT the `@kolu/surface` sense of the word, where a rooted bundle is a composed wire — see src/bundle.ts's header, which is the one place the two could be confused.
//exports: TWO CODE DOORS, and it was three. Three because three GRAPHS: the manifests whole (SolidJS, and behind kolu's a terminal emulator), the browser-safe wire half, and the composition root's rows. Two of those have collapsed into the ROOT, and the reason is that the graph got EMPTIER rather than fuller — the root is one row per plugin with a dynamic `import()` of its browser half, so nothing behind it statically imports a plugin at all and each plugin is its own CHUNK, fetched only when the roster names it. `./bundle` is what a COMPOSITION ROOT reads: the base bundle's ROWS, the loader that mounts them, the `--plugins` patch, and the per-row state report the preferences panel's word is made of. Neither door carries a plugin's code; both SPELL every plugin, because a module specifier a loader resolves and a dynamic import's literal both survive where a static import's is stripped. TWO more entries are routing rather than graphs, because the fence is about a NAME in any grammar: `./all.css` is the plugins' stylesheets chained, and `./testids` is the same routing in a third — a `data-testid` is spent in `@olai/tests`, which may not name a plugin either, and the door is NAMES ONLY so a suite with no browser in it never pulls a component. Both are GENERATED from the rows now (../generate.ts). src/fence.test.ts walks each closure rather than trusting this sentence.
//: WHAT A PLUGIN'S NAME MAY BE SPELLED IN — olai.yml is the build's rows and the only hand-written spelling; generate.ts writes the other three (the browser's rows, the stylesheet chain and the testid merge) out of it; and src/fence.test.ts is what refuses a general package that names a tenant before a reviewer has to notice.
//dependencies: The three plugins, the interface they are written against, and the bridge that mounts them. The plugin dependencies are declared even though nothing here imports one STATICALLY any more: a dynamic `import()` and a loader-resolved specifier are both real edges, and a manifest that did not declare them would be a package whose install could not resolve its own generated rows. `js-yaml` is NOT declared and is not an omission — it is the cordis pin.s, read from the root the way every hydrated package.s runtime dependency is, and `../generate.ts` reads the rows with the same one. `@olai/plugin-api` is the INTERFACE and is a dependency in this direction only — it names no plugin, which is what makes the arrow one-way and the cycle unrepresentable. `@olai/effect-cordis` is the plugin RUNTIME, and this package is one of the two that name it: mounting a bundle is a loader entry and reading a row's state is a registry walk, and both of those are Cordis behind a door that says Effect. `cordis` and `@cordisjs/plugin-loader`/`-include` are NOT named here at all — src/fence.test.ts refuses them in every package but the bridge — and they are hydrated from the npins pin (nix/cordis.nix) into the root node_modules, the way every `@kolu/*` member is, with scripts/check-hydrated-deps.sh holding their versions. `effect` is for the schemas a contributed member is declared in.
